newsitem.title: USA: California house fire that killed nine ruled arson.
newsitem.headline: California house fire that killed nine ruled arson.

text.p: Detectives Tuesday said a fire that swept through a California house, killing nine people, was arson and said a homicide investigation was under way.
Don O'Keefe, a detective sergeant with the San Mateo County Sheriff's office, said a flammable substance was found in the carport where investigators believe the fire started.
"It was deliberately set," O'Keefe said. "Obviously we're considering this a homicide investigation."
O'Keefe said investigators have not identified any suspects.
Five children, aged 5 to 11, and four women, all from the same family, died in the early-morning fire April 26 in East Palo Alto, 50 miles south of San Francisco.
The victims were trapped inside the house by burglar bars bolted on the windows, a common window feature of the neighbourhood, which has a high crime rate.
Firefighters had a hard time getting into the building because a burning car blocked access to the front door and two angry pit bulls barred their way when they tried to go to the back of the house.
Menlo Park Fire District Chief Rick Tye said it was the deadliest fire in the district's 80-year history.
